2611.31341.image_caption: Figure 1 : Before: Misty’s capabilities are predefined, so tasks that need a missing capability cannot be completed. With EvoMisty: The agent autonomously builds required capabilities, optimizes its solutions on user-specified metrics, and distills these solutions into reusable skills.

2611.31475.image_caption: Figure 1 : Overview of SpatialCraft. Phase 1: (A) contrasting rollouts of the same task distills Experiences, each anchored to the active Skill; (B) randomly withholding an Experience across rollouts isolates its effect from task difficulty; (C) proven Experiences are folded into their Skills. Phase 2: the agent (D) retrieves global Experiences per subtask and (E) activates Skills that bring their anchored Experiences.

2611.32093.image_caption: Figure 4 : MARGIN refinement examples across three benchmarks. Real simulator frames illustrate paired execution outcomes on unseen initializations. Top: the original program at matched control steps and termination. Bottom: the MARGIN revision during execution and at termination. The variable t t denotes the executed control step. (a) LIBERO-Pro mug placement. The revision completes placement with 200 fewer steps. (b) LIBERO-90 drawer closure and bowl placement. The revision completes the task with ample execution headroom. (c) Robosuite spill wiping. The revision completes the wipe in a shorter trajectory.

2611.32185.image_caption: Figure 2 : Comparison of paradigms (a–c) against OVOK (d), evolving tools and workflows for robot state estimation.

2611.32196.image_caption: Figure 1 : Agentic video creation and source-conditioned recasting. VideoWeaver [ 37 ] composes generation tools. Direct and adapted Aurora [ 42 ] each edit once; PE Loop revises prompts while returning to the source. RecastAgent chooses both video states and prompts under an independent Critic, consulting frozen design references and experience. The branch diagram is schematic; PE was not run on the illustrated example. All model weights remain frozen.

2611.32390.image_caption: Figure 1: Identical inference-time accuracy can lead to different internalization outcomes. (a) Two experiences generated by GLM-5.2 achieve the same context-conditioned accuracy on AIME25 (20.83%). After 20 steps of on-policy self-distillation, the higher-alignment experience (top) yields 21.11% accuracy, compared with 18.06% for the lower-alignment experience (bottom), a gap of 3.06 percentage points. (b–c) Across 33 candidate experiences, instruction-following accuracy shows almost no correlation with post-distillation accuracy ( ρ = − 0.059 \rho=-0.059 ), whereas gradient alignment on model errors correlates with post-distillation accuracy ( ρ = 0.484 \rho=0.484 ).

2611.32606.image_caption: Figure 3: Overview of one generation g g . Collective: copies of the policy π θ \pi_{\theta} write messages to a shared store, read and cite each other’s messages, and can hand their reading budget to another member, so hubs form on their own; evidence helps ( + ⁣ + ++ ) and arguments mislead ( − ⁣ − -- ). Commit: every member answers with a confidence q q , and the group commits the answer with the most backers, ties going to higher confidence, so the selector only picks among answers that members gave. Compare: the record’s completion tokens set its cost n B n_{B} , the number of independent agents they pay for; the same agents run alone with the same information, and the group is graded against n B n_{B} of them on three levels, one member, their majority vote and pass@ n n , with a margin that splits into accuracy and cost (Equation 1 ). Train: the next generation π g + 1 \pi_{g+1} trains on the outputs that the group’s own protocol accepts, with no teacher and no answer label (collective training), or, when no protocol checks single turns, on the group’s outcome with each member paid its Shapley credit (Section 4.3 ), and controls test the gain: a control trained with the same recipe on base-model turns and, on HiddenBench, single-agent self-training, which trains each agent on its own outputs; a candidate is released only when it outperforms its parent on fresh tasks (Figure 4 ), and the loop repeats. Panel titles give the sections that develop each step.

2611.32951.image_caption: Figure 1 : Harness evolution for video and omnimodal understanding. (a) Video-centric tasks primarily emphasize visual perception, providing a relatively focused space for harness evolution. (b) Omnimodal questions require different combinations of audio, visual, and textual evidence, often with temporal alignment. The resulting interactions among harness strategies make failure attribution and targeted refinement more challenging, motivating modality-aware harness evolution.

2611.31673.image_caption: Figure 1 : From a specialist stack to a coding task. (a) Before: a modality expert, dedicated architecture, labeled data, and a GPU feed a self-configuring framework, nnU-Net [ 10 ] . (b) Now (Build): an unmodified coding agent (Claude Code or Codex CLI) takes only a task description, labeled data, and a CPU to deliver its own segmenter, lifting the exact same test case (CardioMassTTE-1151 [ 33 ] ; yellow: reference, cyan: prediction) from 0.77 to 0.92 Dice and reaching 99% of nnU-Net Dice across 2D tasks. (c) With a quality signal: told scalar True-Dice after each round, the same agent repairs a flawed mask from 0.69 to 0.94 Dice in three rounds. (d) Without a quality signal (quality blind spot): visual self-review raises its 0–100 self-rating from 45 to 65 even as Dice drops from 0.85 to 0.46— seeing is not verifying .

2611.32246.image_caption: Figure 2: Overview of SkillCore. (1) Skill-Scaffolded Demonstrations: Given a user task, a skill retriever selects and loads a relevant skill (e.g., Filter Rows Skill ) into the agent’s context. Guided by the skill, the agent interacts with the environment to produce a successful trajectory of agent actions and environment observations. (2) Scaffolding-Removed Fine-Tuning: We remove the skill scaffold while preserving the task context and subsequent agent actions, yielding scaffold-removed trajectories for supervised fine-tuning that transfer the demonstrated procedure into the model’s parameters. (3) Evaluation: We assess generalizable skill internalization (base vs. fine-tuned agent on the same task without external skill content, judged by an LLM), task-specific skill invocation retention (appropriate skill invocation when task-specific skill content is not provided in context but remains accessible at runtime), and preservation of general coding capability (the auxiliary SWE-bench Verified evaluation).

2611.32480.image_caption: Figure 1: Scripts-first intuition behind VISE. People organize workflows around tools. VISE similarly builds or reuses scripts and derives structural feedback from their implementations to refine SKILL.md .

2611.32576.image_caption: Fig. 3: Overview of the ERDR framework. Training and validation groups support solver evaluation and validation-guided reselection, respectively. (a) The original objective used in solver evaluation and reselection is augmented with inter-group variability and tail risk in solving time. (b) Validation-guided reselection reevaluates candidates to update the solver pool before the next evolution.

2611.33005.image_caption: Figure 5: Answer accuracy by evidence-recall band. Each cell shows its number of questions; hatched cells contain fewer than ten.

2611.33119.image_caption: Figure 1: MetaFORGE: An automated meta-learning skill-refinement architecture. MetaFORGE optimizes LLM coding skills through execution-grounded feedback. Generated MPI C code is compiled, statically analyzed, executed, and scored using Eq. ( 1 ). Diagnostics and reward trends are converted into a textual gradient for skill-prompt rewriting, while iteration artifacts are stored, distilled, indexed, and retrieved as long-term memory, enabling future updates to reuse prior reward-improving strategies.

2611.31307.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of MIMPA. A malicious insider agent plants malicious payloads during a normal planting task, which are later retrieved to induce incorrect answers in the target task.

2611.31511.image_caption: Figure 1: ID and OOD success rate matrices for LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus (mean across perturbation categories). Each cell C ⁡ ( k , i ) C(k,i) reports the success rate of checkpoint θ k \theta_{k} (row) on task T i T_{i} (column); only valid cells with k ≥ i k\geq i are shown. For the first row of subplots, the ID cells are shown; for the second, the mean of the cells across the OOD categories is shown. For ID, the dense, high-SR lower triangles indicate near-zero forgetting across all four suites, whereas for OOD the lower-triangular regions show a clear drop in performance: most cells are close to zero, while some isolated spikes of active cells (under-diagonal cells with SR > 0 >0 ) remain, revealing OOD forgetting.

2611.31539.image_caption: Figure 1: Estimated Bounds and Confidence Intervals for NetworkX Experiment. Confidence sets are pointwise for each minimum speedup threshold and agent, with α = 0.1 \alpha=0.1 . The bolded line denotes the midpoint of our estimated bounds and confidence sets.

2611.31595.image_caption: Figure 8: Step type × \times position bias interaction. Darker blue indicates more severe under-rating (negative bias), whereas warm orange/peach indicates over-rating (positive bias). Computation, verification, and restatement steps in late positions show the strongest under-rating.
